subject: What remains — the self that does not die
place: The inner self, beyond the body
events: The body grows old and falls away
The self does not die, for it was never born
What remains is the self — the realization from within
grounding_notes: The self is not the body, not the name, not the story.
The self is the one who watches, who knows, who is.
The self does not die because it was never born.
The answer to Who am I? needs no words.

included_characters.role_in_chapter: Protagonist — the one who grows old
The self that does not die

chapter_summary: The seeker grows old, and the body grows tired, and the world goes on with its noise and its hurry — but the self does not grow old, does not grow tired, remains whole and silent and free. When the body at last falls away, the seeker does not fear, for the self is not the body, not the name, not the story, but the one who watches, who knows, who is — and that self does not die, because it was never born. What remains is not the person but the self, the realization from within, the truth that was always there, waiting to be remembered.
